title: Berlin Rent Increase - Quick Summary
items: **A new Mietspiegel landed on 28 May 2026**, so this is the busy season for rent letters. The Berliner Mietspiegel 2026 is a qualified Mietspiegel under section 558d BGB, covers about 1.6 million flats and puts the median net cold rent at **7.71 euro per square metre**, up from 7.21 in the 2024 edition.

**Four separate limits, and they are independent.** The 15 per cent over three years, the Mietspiegel value for your flat, the 12 and 15 month clocks, and the form of the letter. A demand can be fine on the money and dead on the date.

**Berlin is a 15 per cent city**, not 20. Section 558(3) BGB allows a state to cut the national ceiling in a tight market and Berlin did it through the Kappungsgrenzenverordnung of 14 March 2023. The base is the rent you paid three years before the rise starts.

**The crossover almost nobody works out:** the 15 per cent only binds if you already pay **less than about 87 per cent of your Mietspiegel value**. At the median 7.71 that is **6.70 euro per square metre**. Above it, the Mietspiegel is your real ceiling and the percentage is decoration.

**Two dates beat the number.** You have until the end of the second calendar month after the letter arrives to agree, and the higher rent starts at the beginning of the third. A letter arriving 10 September 2026 means 30 November and 1 December.

**Silence is not agreement**, but it opens the landlord's three months to sue for your consent. Agreeing in writing to the part that holds up, and saying plainly you do not agree above it, is usually the better move.

**Modernisation is a different track.** Section 559 allows 8 per cent of the work's cost per year, capped at 3 euro per square metre in six years, or 2 euro if the rent was under 7. It needs no agreement from you, and neither does an operating cost adjustment under section 560.
**Check the contract type first.** A Staffelmiete blocks both a comparable rent rise and a modernisation rise while it runs, and an Indexmiete excludes a comparable rent rise altogether.
